unit.title: Sequence of Tenses
unit.subtitle: Correlación temporal: matching the subjunctive to the main clause

grammar.title: Choosing the right subjunctive tense
grammar.intro: Once a verb triggers the subjunctive, you still have to pick which subjunctive. That choice is governed by the tense of the main clause and by timing — whether the subordinate action is simultaneous with, or prior to, the main one. This is the correlación temporal, and getting it right is what separates B2 from C1.

sections.heading: Present / future main → present subjunctive
sections.body: If the main verb is in the present, future or is an imperative, a simultaneous or later action takes the present subjunctive. If the subordinate action is already completed, switch to the perfect subjunctive (haya + participle).

ex.en: I want you to come to the meeting.

sections.heading: Past / conditional main → imperfect subjunctive
sections.body: If the main verb is in the imperfect, preterite, conditional or pluperfect, a simultaneous or later action takes the imperfect subjunctive (viniera / viniese). If it's prior to the main clause, use the pluperfect subjunctive (hubiera venido).

ex.en: I wanted you to come with me.
I didn't think you had already come.

sections.heading: Simultaneity vs anteriority
sections.body: The rule of thumb: keep the simple subjunctive (present or imperfect) for actions at the same time or later, and use a compound subjunctive (perfect or pluperfect) for actions that happened before the main clause. Anchor the tense to the main clause, then adjust for timing.

ex.en: I was hoping you had called earlier.

takeaways: Present/future main clause → present subjunctive (or perfect subjunctive if already completed).
Past/conditional main clause → imperfect subjunctive (or pluperfect subjunctive if prior).
Simultaneous or later = simple subjunctive; earlier = compound subjunctive.
Quiero que vengas ↔ Quería que vinieras: the main tense drags the subordinate one back.

mistakes.why: A past main clause (quería) requires the imperfect subjunctive, not the present.
pidió is past, so the subordinate verb must be imperfect subjunctive: llegara.

mistakes.r: Me alegra que hayas venido ayer.
mistakes.why: With a present main clause, a completed past action takes the perfect subjunctive.

exercises.prompt: Quería que ___ conmigo a la reunión.
exercises.prompt_en: I wanted you to come with me to the meeting.
exercises.no: A past main clause (quería) pulls the subjunctive back to the imperfect: vinieras.

exercises.prompt: Me sorprende que todavía no ___ nada al respecto.
exercises.prompt_en: I'm surprised they haven't said anything about it yet.
exercises.ok: ¡Exacto! Presente + acción ya completada → perfecto de subjuntivo.
exercises.no: Present main clause + a completed action → perfect subjunctive: hayan dicho.

exercises.prompt: Build: “I asked them to arrive on time.”
exercises.no: “Les pedí que llegaran a tiempo” — the past main verb needs the imperfect subjunctive.

exercises.prompt: Dudo que ellos ya ___ la noticia. (recibir)
exercises.prompt_en: I doubt they've already received the news.
exercises.hint: Present main clause + an already-completed action → perfect subjunctive.
exercises.ok: ¡Bien! presente + ya → perfecto de subjuntivo: hayan recibido.
exercises.no: It's “hayan recibido”: a present main clause with a completed action takes the perfect subjunctive.

exercises.prompt: Match each main clause to the subjunctive tense it requires.

exercises.translation: I was hoping you would call me last night.
exercises.no: It was: “Esperaba que me llamaras anoche.” (esperaba → llamaras).

exercises.scenario: A friend admits she left you waiting 🚉

lines.speaker: Laura
lines.es: Al final no te esperé en la estación, lo siento.
lines.en: In the end I didn't wait for you at the station, sorry.

options.text: Pues me habría gustado que me avisaras.
Pues me habría gustado que me avises.
Pues me habría gustado que me avisabas.

exercises.no: “Me habría gustado” (conditional) demands the imperfect subjunctive: que me avisaras.

exercises.say: Quería que vinieras a la reunión.
exercises.en: I wanted you to come to the meeting.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the rhythm of “Quería que vinieras a la reunión.”

vocab.en: I didn't think you had come
